summary: TerraMatch is an open web tool that finds and scores Earth analog sites for Moon and Mars landing sites using measurements instead of visual resemblance. We measure the same ten physical and chemical properties (terrain and slopes, surface texture, brightness, temperature, thermal inertia, minerals, dryness, water and ice, dust and wind, radar roughness, plus an AI landform-shape score) on Earth, the Moon and Mars from open NASA, ESA, CSA and JAXA data, and rank every pair by how well it fits a mission goal (landing, search for life, permanent base, dust). It addresses the challenge by screening all 70,718 land cells on Earth instead of a handful of famous sites, and by reporting exactly which properties match and where an analog breaks (gravity, atmosphere, radiation, biology). This matters because better-chosen analogs make hardware tests and astronaut training for Artemis and future Mars missions cheaper and more reliable.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TerraMatch answers: which places on Earth behave like Moon-base and Mars landing sites, and in what ways? Instead of picking analogs by how they look, it measures the same properties on all three worlds and scores each Earth-target pair. Every result shows its data source and the reasons behind the score, including where the match fails.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Ten properties are computed the same way for Earth, the Moon and Mars: terrain and slopes (common 200 m grid), surface texture, brightness, temperature (each body's relative hot/cold position plus day-night swing), thermal inertia, minerals (as mineral families), dryness, water and ice, dust and wind, radar roughness, and a landform-shape score from an AI vision model (DINOv2 on hillshades, 72 views).

2. Per-property similarity = exp(-difference / scale).

3. Mission profiles (landing, search for life, permanent base, dust) weight the properties. A pair is ranked only when at least 50% of the mission's weight has data on both sides, so missing data never helps a site.

4. A global screen with NASA MERRA-2 scores every one of 70,718 land cells (~50 km) against targets such as Jezero Crater; the best regions are then analysed in full detail.

5. Results are shown in a web app with Dashboard, Explore, Analysis, Ranking and Report views.

KEY FINDINGS

- The method was never told which sites are famous analogs, yet Atacama ranks in the top 0.2% of Earth's land for Jezero, and the Antarctic plateau (Dome A) in the top 0.1% for a lunar polar base (Haworth).

- It surfaced regions not commonly used as analogs: Kumtag Desert/Lop Nur (China) 66% for Arcadia Planitia, northern Ellesmere Island (Canada) 65% for Haworth (Moon), Nubian Desert (Sudan) 64% for Arcadia Planitia.

- Egypt's Western Desert ranks first for all three Mars rover sites: White Desert for Jezero (EMIT detects calcite, minerals match 100%), Gilf Kebir for Oxia Planum (kaolinite clays on very flat plains, terrain 91%), Gebel Kamil for Gale (same clay family, AI landform similarity 92%). It breaks on brightness, dust and temperature (Egyptian nights are ~100 K warmer than Gale's).

- L-band radar (JAXA ALOS PALSAR) reveals a buried drainage network near Gebel Kamil that is invisible in Sentinel-2 optical imagery. This makes the area a process-analog test field for Mars subsurface radars (SHARAD, MARSIS).

- Lunar polar matches are weaker, as expected: nothing on Earth is ~20 K cold and airless.

BENEFITS

Mission planners and researchers get a reproducible, data-based way to choose where to test rovers, radars and habitat technology, and an honest list of what each analog cannot reproduce (gravity, atmosphere, radiation, biology).

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

A searchable, open reference of Earth analog sites for the Moon and Mars that can grow as new data and mission targets are added.

TOOLS

Live app: https://terramatch-five.vercel.app/ (hosted on Vercel). Code: https://github.com/KarimAshraf04/TerraMatch

Stack: [list: e.g. Python / geospatial libraries / JavaScript framework for the web app]. AI model: DINOv2 for landform features. Validation: 22 automated tests covering the maths, data checks against known facts, and the AI model.
